summary: Walker County, TX Texas Forest Service site listed as gone; a 1935 NGS description on the Forest Lookouts page places a survey mark 49.2 feet from a lookout tower on agency land.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Texas list; no removal date in the sources read

events.note: NGS station description (PID BL1669) written in 1935 refers to an existing lookout tower on the site

evidence.supports: Fails (Mossy Grove) listed in Walker County at 30.81111, -95.70389, as a tower that is gone
agency is the Texas Forest Service
station description written in 1935 by the Coast and Geodetic Survey
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1935

evidence.supports: station is about 10 miles northwest of Huntsville
station is on land owned by the Texas Forest Service
evidence.quote: ON LAND OWNED BY THE TEXAS FOREST SERVICE

evidence.supports: mark is 49.2 feet north of the northeast leg of the lookout tower, so a tower is referred to on the site
evidence.quote: THE MARK IS SET 49.2 FEET N OF THE NE LEG OF THE LOOKOUT TOWER

evidence.supports: station is about 15 miles southeast of Madisonville
station is listed on the USGS Crabbs Prairie quadrangle, dated 1976
page reproduces a National Geodetic Survey station description

notes_for_editor: Two sources, and the only site-specific text is the NGS station description reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page. That description refers to a lookout tower but does not name it, give its height or design, or date its removal. The page's header number #25 was not interpreted. WebSearch returned only 2022-2023 Walker County wildfire news and nothing about a Mossy Grove tower. Not verified whether the 1935 NGS mark and the Texas list's coordinates refer to the same hill.
